author: Mark Atwood
text: INVESTIGATED (worker8, 2026-09-09) — confirmed real, and confirmed NOT a leaf bead. FINDINGS: (1) The target code python/src/lichen/node.py::_reannounce_capabilities_to_new_root (main:1182-1224) exists on main but NOT on beads-worker-8 (I am 56 commits behind); it POSTs a COSE_Sign1 capability announcement as a bare aiocoap Message (NON) via wrap_coap + node.send — zero OSCORE. (2) The node has NO EDHOC initiator wiring anywhere (grep: no EdhocInitiator/SecureDatagramChannel in node.py/node_channel.py); the re-announce bypasses the entire coap.secure stack. (3) The project's own root CapabilityAnnounceResource.render_post returns 4.01 oscore_required for plaintext (capability_announce.py:184-189), so the re-announce is dead-on-arrival against in-repo root. (4) The 99sg.2 test file (test_node_capability_reannounce.py) referenced in its close reason is ABSENT from main — lost in the i72x/q6ko store corruption (bead rul5). FIX SHAPE (clear but architectural, ~multi-file): wrap the node's NodeChannel in coap.secure.SecureDatagramChannel (factory create_secure_channel exists) and route the re-announce through it, establishing an EDHOC pairwise context to the new root. Open design questions that are Mark's call per this bead's own text: (a) EDHOC context lifecycle — when/where to establish toward a brand-new root (root is not yet a pinned/known peer at re-announce time; TOFU vs pre-provisioned); (b) fire-and-forget NON re-announce vs the secure channel's request/response model; (c) interim behavior until EDHOC lands (silently skip? queue? log-and-drop?). RECOMMEND: Mark make the interim design decision (the bead names this as a valid resolution), then decompose the EDHOC-client integration into leaf slices. Releasing — not claiming the EDHOC internals/integration, which borders the human-only oscore/EDHOC bar.
